title: Seventh Word Satans Deception And The Dialogue Over Talisman Medicine And Ticket

questions.question: Who came to the soldier after some time?
questions.answer: A tricky, bad-looking man came to him.

questions.question: From which side did that man come?
questions.answer: He came from the left.

questions.question: What kinds of things did the man bring?
questions.answer: He brought fancy things, pretty pictures, make-believe ideas, and drinks that make people lose control.

questions.question: What fun did the man invite the soldier to have?
questions.answer: He wanted him to drink, party, look at girls’ pictures, hear music, and eat tasty food.

questions.question: What was the soldier quietly saying?
questions.answer: He was saying a special prayer-like protection.

questions.question: How did the tricky man talk about that recitation?
questions.answer: He said it was meaningless and told him to stop.

questions.question: What was the thing in the soldier’s hand?
questions.answer: It was medicine.

questions.question: Why did the man tell the soldier to throw the medicine away?
questions.answer: He said the soldier was fine and should just enjoy himself.

questions.question: What paper did the soldier have?
questions.answer: He had a travel pass and a food card.

questions.question: What did the man tell him to do with that paper?
questions.answer: He told him to rip it up.

questions.question: How did the man try to get the soldier to follow him?
questions.answer: He used many tricks and smooth words.

questions.question: Did the soldier stay strong right away?
questions.answer: No. He started to be pulled in a little.

questions.question: What lesson is given about people?
questions.answer: People can be fooled.

questions.question: What happened suddenly from the right side?
questions.answer: A loud warning voice came.

questions.question: What was the first warning from the voice?
questions.answer: It told him not to be tricked.

questions.question: What was the soldier told to ask the trickster to do first?
questions.answer: He should ask him to stop the lion behind him.

questions.question: What else was the trickster challenged to remove?
questions.answer: The gallows in front and the pain on both sides.

questions.question: What last big problem was the trickster challenged to stop?
questions.answer: He was challenged to stop the journey ahead.

questions.question: If the trickster could not do these things, what should he do?
questions.answer: He should keep quiet.

questions.question: Whom was the soldier told to speak like?
questions.answer: He was told to speak like the Allah-guided man from before.

questions.question: What kind of person does the passage show the new man to be?
questions.answer: He is sneaky and harmful.

questions.question: What did he use to tempt the soldier?
questions.answer: He used pretty-looking pleasures and exciting things.

questions.question: What did the man ask about the soldier’s quiet words?
questions.answer: He asked what he was repeating softly.

questions.question: What answer did the soldier give?
questions.answer: He said it was a protective talisman.

questions.question: What does the bad man’s answer show about his attitude?
questions.answer: He did not respect it and wanted the soldier to stop using it.

questions.question: What did the soldier say the item in his hand was for?
questions.answer: It was a medicine.

questions.question: What wrong idea did the man give about the medicine?
questions.answer: He acted as if the soldier had no sickness or hurt.

questions.question: What were the two papers for?
questions.answer: One was for travel, and one was for food supplies.

questions.question: Why did the man say those papers were not needed?
questions.answer: He wanted the soldier to think only about the nice time right now.

questions.question: How much was the soldier affected by the trickster?
questions.answer: He was a little fooled by him.

questions.question: What extra example is given to show this can happen?
questions.answer: The speaker says he was also fooled by similar tricks.

questions.question: From which side did the warning come?
questions.answer: It came from the right.

questions.question: How strong did the warning sound?
questions.answer: It sounded very strong, like thunder.

questions.question: What big test was the trickster given?
questions.answer: He was told to prove he could remove all the soldier’s dangers.

questions.question: Name one danger the voice mentioned.
questions.answer: One was the lion behind him.

questions.question: Name another danger the voice mentioned.
questions.answer: Another was the gallows in front of him.

questions.question: What should the soldier do instead of following him?
questions.answer: He should reject him and follow the guidance of the Allah-inspired man.

questions.question: What was the soldier doing when the sneaky man came?
questions.answer: He was quietly reciting something.

questions.question: How did the man try to change the soldier’s focus?
questions.answer: He tried to pull him toward pleasure and fun.

questions.question: Which five kinds of enjoyment did the man mention?
questions.answer: Drinking, partying, looking at women’s pictures, listening to music, and eating good food.

questions.question: When asked about his recitation, what simple answer did the soldier give?
questions.answer: He said it was a talisman.

questions.question: What was the man’s reaction to the talisman?
questions.answer: He mocked it and wanted it stopped.

questions.question: What did the soldier call the object in his hand?
questions.answer: He called it medicine.

questions.question: What reason did the trickster give for throwing it away?
questions.answer: He claimed the soldier was healthy.

questions.question: What two things did the marked paper stand for?
questions.answer: It stood for travel help and food help.

questions.question: Why did the man say the soldier should destroy the paper?
questions.answer: He wanted him to ignore the road ahead.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the man’s methods?
questions.answer: It says he used many clever tricks.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier because of those tricks?
questions.answer: He became somewhat persuaded.

questions.question: What general truth is stated after that?
questions.answer: Human beings can be deceived.

questions.question: What broke into the scene next?
questions.answer: A powerful warning voice.

questions.question: What was the first thing the voice told the soldier to say back?
questions.answer: He should ask the trickster to defeat the lion.

questions.question: After the lion, what should he ask about the gallows?
questions.answer: He should ask him to take it away.

questions.question: What should he ask about the pains on both sides?
questions.answer: He should ask him to stop them.

questions.question: What should he ask about the road ahead?
questions.answer: He should ask him to prevent the journey.

questions.question: Was the man who came to the soldier presented as honest or deceitful?
questions.answer: He was presented as deceitful.

questions.question: What details in the passage help show that he was deceitful?
questions.answer: His sneaky look, his tempting items, and his tricky talk show it.

questions.question: What did he want the soldier to do first with him?
questions.answer: He wanted him to go have fun and celebrate.

questions.question: What question did he ask about the soldier’s quiet words?
questions.answer: He asked what he was saying softly.

questions.question: What answer did the soldier give about those words?
questions.answer: They were a talisman.

questions.question: How did the man treat something meant to help the soldier?
questions.answer: He spoke against it as if it had no value.

questions.question: What second helpful thing did the man attack?
questions.answer: He attacked the medicine.

questions.question: What third helpful thing did the man attack?
questions.answer: He attacked the ticket and food card.

questions.question: What pattern do you see in what the man says?
questions.answer: He tries to make the soldier throw away every useful aid.

questions.question: What sentence in the passage gives a warning for all people?
questions.answer: It teaches that people can be fooled.

questions.question: What personal example is added to strengthen that warning?
questions.answer: The speaker says he also was tricked in a similar way.

questions.question: What kind of voice came from the right?
questions.answer: A loud, commanding voice came.

questions.question: What did the voice tell the soldier not to do?
questions.answer: It told him not to be deceived.

questions.question: What danger was behind the soldier?
questions.answer: A lion was behind him.

questions.question: What danger was in front of the soldier?
questions.answer: A gallows was in front of him.

questions.question: What dangers were at the soldier’s sides?
questions.answer: Things were hurting him on both sides.

questions.question: What lay ahead of the soldier?
questions.answer: A journey lay ahead.

questions.question: What should the soldier do if the trickster cannot solve any of this?
questions.answer: He should tell him to be quiet and not follow him.

questions.question: When the sneaky man arrived, what did he bring that looked attractive?
questions.answer: He brought decorated things that looked pleasing and exciting.

questions.question: What kind of life did the man invite the soldier into at that moment?
questions.answer: A life of fun, pleasure, and carelessness.

questions.question: What did the soldier say he was reciting?
questions.answer: A talisman.

questions.question: Why did the trickster dislike the recitation?
questions.answer: He thought it would interrupt the fun he wanted.

questions.question: What did the soldier say he was carrying in his hand?
questions.answer: Medicine.

questions.question: What false claim did the trickster make about the soldier’s condition?
questions.answer: He said the soldier was fine and needed no treatment.

questions.question: What paper with marks did the soldier have?
questions.answer: He had a ticket and a rations card.

questions.question: What season did the man mention when trying to mislead him?
questions.answer: He mentioned spring.

questions.question: Did the man use just one trick or many tricks?
questions.answer: He used many tricks.

questions.question: How did those tricks affect the soldier?
questions.answer: They almost drew him in.

questions.question: What warning about human nature is stated clearly?
questions.answer: A person can be deceived.

questions.question: What interrupted the man’s tempting speech?
questions.answer: A voice like thunder interrupted it.

questions.question: What one-word warning did the voice begin with?
questions.answer: It began with a warning to watch out.

questions.question: What four impossible jobs was the trickster challenged to do?
questions.answer: Kill the lion, remove the gallows, stop the wounds, and prevent the journey.

questions.question: What should happen if he cannot do them?
questions.answer: He should stop talking.

questions.question: Whose way of speaking should the soldier follow?
questions.answer: He should follow the way of the Khidr-like, Allah-inspired man.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the man who came from the left: helper or tempter?
questions.answer: He is a tempter.

questions.question: How can you tell he is a tempter?
questions.answer: He offers sinful fun and tells the soldier to give up helpful things.

questions.question: What did he invite the soldier to enjoy with him?
questions.answer: He invited him to drinking, entertainment, pictures, music, and tasty food.

questions.question: What spiritual thing was the soldier using with his mouth?
questions.answer: He was using a talisman.

questions.question: What healing thing was the soldier holding?
questions.answer: He was holding medicine.

questions.question: What preparing things did the soldier also have?
questions.answer: He had a travel ticket and a ration card.

questions.question: What three helpful things did the tempter try to get rid of?
questions.answer: The talisman, the medicine, and the papers for the journey.

questions.question: What does that tell us about his true goal?
questions.answer: He wanted to leave the soldier unprotected and unready.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the poor soldier’s response?
questions.answer: He was partly convinced.

questions.question: What larger lesson is taught right after this?
questions.answer: Even people can be tricked by clever lies.

questions.question: What personal confession is included?
questions.answer: The speaker says he too was tricked by such lies.

questions.question: What came from the right side at once?
questions.answer: A strong warning voice came.

questions.question: What was the soldier first told to remember?
questions.answer: He was told not to let himself be deceived.

questions.question: What question should the soldier put to the trickster about the lion?
questions.answer: He should ask whether the trickster can destroy it.

questions.question: What question should he put about the gallows?
questions.answer: He should ask whether it can be taken away.

questions.question: What should he ask about the pains on his sides?
questions.answer: He should ask whether they can be stopped.

questions.question: What should he ask about the road ahead?
questions.answer: He should ask whether the journey can be prevented.
